findings.title: listRecentAuditEvents 'actor' param queries the 'subject' column (D68 pre-scoped #5 / D69 SO-21 still open)
findings.description: The contract (`packages/domain/src/runtime/store-contract.ts:181-186`) advertises `actor?: string` as a filter, and D66 spec §2.1 documents `actor` as 'the actor'. But the SQL impl in runtime-store.ts:625-627 maps `actor` to `eq(auditEvents.subject, actor)`. Semantically `subject` is what was acted on (tool name / runId / owner-id string depending on caller) — there is no dedicated `actor` column. Per D68 pre-scoped #5 + D70 SO-1: schema needs a dedicated `actor` column. Without it, owner-routes/audit-fatigue.ts:75 'cross-actor replay rejected' check matches against subject tokens that other callers (wechat-inbound-butler.ts:583 'subject: String(def.name)') already overwrote for other purposes — false-positive 403s.
findings.evidence:
runtime-store.ts:625-627: `if (actor !== undefined) conditions.push(eq(auditEvents.subject, actor))`
store-contract.ts:181-186: `readonly listRecentAuditEvents: (input: { readonly actor?: string; ... })`
audit-service.ts:49: `Filters compose with AND semantics: actor (matches the \`subject\` column)`
audit_events schema (migration 0002 line 68-78) has NO actor column — only run_id/conversation_id/action/subject/detail/created_at/correlation_id (0013)
findings.fix_hint: Add migration 0014 adding `actor text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'` column + index `audit_events_actor_idx`. Update schema.ts (auditEvents table) + appendAuditEvent contract (add `actor` field) + ALL ~20 emit sites to populate actor (e.g., wechatIn-user, telegram-update, schedule-worker, owner-handle). Then runtime-store.ts:626 swaps to `eq(auditEvents.actor, actor)`.

findings.title: audit-fatigue.ts:70 raw.req.json catch swallows JSON parse errors silently into 'invalid body' 400
findings.description: audit-fatigue.ts:70 `await c.req.json().catch(() => null)` returns null on JSON parse failure. The 400 response says 'invalid body: expected { sequence_event_ids: string[] } (1-1000 ids)' — but the actual root cause was a JSON parse error, not a schema error. Owner sees misleading error. Cross-actor replay check happens later (line 101-103) — if replay succeeds, no log of the parse error for operator diagnostics.
findings.evidence:
audit-fatigue.ts:70-73: `const raw: unknown = await c.req.json().catch(() => null); if (!isReplayBody(raw)) { return c.json({ error: 'invalid body: expected { sequence_event_ids: string[] } (1-${MAX_REPLAY_BATCH} ids)' }, 400) }`
Hono `req.json()` throws on parse error; the catch silently returns null without logging
findings.fix_hint: Wrap parse with explicit error logging: `const raw: unknown = await c.req.json().catch((err) => { console.error('[audit-fatigue] body parse failed:', err); return null })`. Differentiate 'parse error' vs 'schema error' in response: `{ error: parse_failed ? '请求体不是合法 JSON' : '请求体缺少 sequence_event_ids' }`.
